current.section_name: General Service to Service Communication Security
current.text: Verify that an encrypted protocol such as TLS is used for all inbound and outbound connections to and from the application, including monitoring systems, management tools, remote access and SSH, middleware, databases, mainframes, partner systems, or external APIs. The server must not fall back to insecure or unencrypted protocols.

master.text: Verify that an encrypted protocol such as TLS is used for all inbound and outbound connections to and from the application, including monitoring systems, management tools, remote access and SSH, middleware, databases, mainframes, partner systems, or external APIs. predecessors.text: Verify that encrypted communications such as TLS is used for all inbound and outbound connections, including for management ports, monitoring, authentication, API, or web service calls, database, cloud, serverless, mainframe, external, and partner connections. The server must not fall back to insecure or unencrypted protocols.

Verify the application encrypts communications between components, particularly when these components are in different containers, systems, sites, or cloud providers. ([C3](https://owasp.org/www-project-proactive-controls/#div-numbering))

summaries.body:
ASVS 5.0.0 V12.3.1 is carried forward from 4.0.3 V9.2.2 and covers V1.9.1. V9.2.2 required encrypted communications such as TLS for all inbound and outbound connections, including management ports, monitoring, authentication, API or web service calls, database, cloud, serverless, mainframe, external, and partner connections, with no fallback to insecure protocols. V1.9.1 required encrypting communications between components, especially across containers, systems, sites, or cloud providers. The mapping records MODIFIED, moved from v4.0.3-9.2.2, covers v4.0.3-1.9.1.

On 2019-02-24 tghosth applied C3 proactive-control changes to V1.9.1. In 4.x the V12.3.1 slot was Files: ryan.goltry’s 2019-03-05 clarity edit and tghosth’s May 2019 Files-Resources updates are that chapter. Mapping and V9.2.2 are the reliable origin; the git timeline is noisy.

The 5.0 text keeps encrypted inbound and outbound connections with no fallback, and lists monitoring systems, management tools, remote access and SSH, middleware, databases, mainframes, partner systems, or external APIs. Cloud/serverless wording from V9.2.2 is not restated. The mapping labels that MODIFIED. On 2022-02-10 tghosth started reworking V9 Communications. Files-chapter commits on this ID did not rewrite this control.
